MY WEATHER JOURNAL

How to Observe the Weather

Look at the sky and notice evidence of wind from a safe indoor spot.

Look, then try.

Choose a closed window with a grown-up. Record the date and time, then describe what you can see. If you cannot tell what the weather is doing, say so instead of guessing.

Start drawing and writing below

Open the worksheet to print or save

Observe with a grown-up from a safe indoor spot. Never look directly at the sun. Stay indoors during storms. For the toy shelter, test over a tray with adult help and keep devices dry.

Use a finger, stylus or mouse in each drawing box. Type below it, or ask a grown-up to write your words. Your work stays in this tab. Save before refreshing or leaving.

ACTIVITY 1

My observation spot

Draw the view through your window.

ACTIVITY 2

Evidence of wind

Look for leaves or a flag. Describe what they do.

Your ideas belong here. There is no score.

What are we learning?

An observation uses evidence. Moving leaves can show wind, but a still picture cannot tell us everything about the weather.
